mine_p02_001.speaker: narrator
mine_p02_001.text: On Day 444, the public gate of Vermilion Hollows opened at the same hour as the bakery. Lin Yue could smell the first trays while she waited beside people whose boots carried yesterday's red grit. Qiao Min arrived carrying a cup rather than a ceremonial staff. She drank before speaking. Today's visitors could enter the cleared receiving gallery under an escort. Nobody could pass the lower timber line, borrow a worker's key, or take a sample merely because the visitor register contained their name.

mine_p02_002.speaker: narrator
mine_p02_002.text: The forewoman pointed to the boards beyond the gate. One listed work areas, another people on duty, and a third the routes closed for inspection. Their edges were worn by fingers. Lin had expected an impressive map of the mountain. Instead she found directions to the latrine, a reminder about empty carts, and a name crossed out because its owner had gone home with a fever. The mine's first claim on her attention was a living person who should not have been underground that morning.

mine_p02_003.speaker: narrator
mine_p02_003.text: A porter asked whether the fever had come from the seam. Qiao said the clinician had not diagnosed a cause and the man was resting away from work. She would not turn uncertainty into a story about the mountain. The porter looked disappointed, then asked where his replacement stood. That question received a name and a time. Lin noticed how quickly a mysterious explanation could consume the practical answer somebody needed. She also noticed Qiao's hand trembling slightly as she set down her empty cup.

mine_p02_004.speaker: narrator
mine_p02_004.text: The forewoman had worked through part of the previous night after a cart lost its brake peg. She was handing the morning inspection to Fan Luwei, the timber engineer, rather than pretending wakefulness was a permanent qualification. He wore a leather apron over a coat patched beneath the elbows. His first question concerned the replacement peg. His second concerned the person who had fitted it. Lin watched Qiao answer both and then leave the active inspection lane. Authority had not made her fatigue harmless.

mine_p02_005.speaker: narrator
mine_p02_005.text: Fan introduced the cleared gallery by its ordinary features. The lamps had separate oil supplies. A bell wire reached the surface attendant. The floor sloped toward a drain which could be checked without entering the sealed workings. Timber marks recorded inspection dates, not promises that wood could never fail. Lin read the nearest date aloud when asked. Fan corrected her final digit. She had mistaken an old knot in the board for part of the number. He let her look again before continuing.

mine_p02_006.speaker: narrator
mine_p02_006.text: Beyond the gallery, a faint ticking came from the rock. It resembled a spoon tapping a bowl, irregular and almost domestic. Lin's attention went toward it. Fan's went toward the visitors behind her. He asked everyone to keep the same walking interval while he examined a loose rope post. The sound could wait. Lin moved back to the marked standing place, embarrassed by how readily she had turned toward an unexplained noise. An interesting seam did not suspend the hazards around a familiar footpath.

mine_p02_007.speaker: narrator
mine_p02_007.text: A worker named Ma Lian brought the rope post's fastening from the tool room. She was not a cultivator and did not apologize for that. She asked Fan whether he wanted the existing bolt cleaned or replaced. He chose replacement after showing the worn thread. Lin could understand the visible defect without pretending to know the fastening's rating. Ma fitted the new piece, and Fan checked it before reopening the short section. The inspection had produced a small change which would matter to every cart using that corner.

mine_p02_008.speaker: narrator
mine_p02_008.text: At the receiving alcove, three assistants waited for assignments. One would accompany the stair inspection, one would observe the ventilation indicators, and one would compare yesterday's work tickets with the public duty board. Each had a qualified lead. None would grant entry into a closed heading or authorize a machine test. Fan offered Lin one bounded assistant's turn if she wished to help. The task ended before noon. Choosing it would give her different observations, not a general certificate to inspect the mine.

mine_p02_009.speaker: narrator
mine_p02_009.text: Lin asked whether refusing the turn would delay her own clearance. Fan said the visitor clearance was independent of unpaid assistance. Qiao had already arranged the escort. The offered turn carried the posted assistant's fee, and a worker could take it if Lin preferred to remain a visitor. She liked the distinction and disliked how surprised she was to hear it. Too many earlier invitations had become duties once she expressed interest. Here she could ask about the work before deciding whether it belonged to her morning.

mine_clearance_choice.speaker: narrator
mine_clearance_choice.text: The three leads described what they actually needed. Ma wanted a second pair of eyes on marked stair treads while she controlled the barrier. Ventilation keeper Ou Sheng needed somebody to record indicator positions without touching the valves. Ticket clerk Ren Tao wanted a patient reader who would leave private wage figures closed. Lin weighed a sore knee on steep steps, the temptation of strange air, and the quieter pressure of another person's handwriting. Each task had something she could do and something she had to leave to its owner.

choices.text: Assist Ma with the permitted stair observations.
Record Ou's ventilation indicators under his direction.
Compare public task tickets with Ren, keeping wage pages closed.

mine_clearance_stairs.speaker: narrator
mine_clearance_stairs.text: Lin accepted the stair assistant's turn. Ma gave her a chalk pencil and showed which marks belonged to yesterday's inspection. Their job was to read those marks, compare the visible treads, and report discrepancies from the cleared landing. They would not load a doubtful step with a human body. The chalk remained mine property and would return to the tool tray. Lin repeated the limit, more slowly than the task seemed to require. Ma nodded as though precision before work was ordinary courtesy rather than evidence of fear.

mine_p02_stairs_002.speaker: narrator
mine_p02_stairs_002.text: The first flight descended only to another cleared landing. Its handrail smelled of fresh linseed oil. Ma tested each permitted fastening with her own rated tool while Lin read the numbered treads. Two numbers had been obscured by a cart scrape. Lin marked that as unreadable instead of guessing. A worker waiting above them sighed at the delay. Ma asked him to use the other cleared stair. He did, carrying his empty basket with an expression which promised a complaint later.

mine_p02_stairs_003.speaker: narrator
mine_p02_stairs_003.text: Halfway down, Lin saw a pale strip beneath the edge of the seventh tread. She thought it was fresh wood. Ma asked her to describe it without naming the cause. The strip moved when a droplet fell from the roof, and Lin realized it was a folded piece of packing paper lodged against the grain. She felt foolish. Ma removed it with the area closed, then showed the actual grain around the fastener. The exercise had cost a minute and prevented a confident mistake from becoming an inspection finding.

mine_p02_stairs_004.speaker: narrator
mine_p02_stairs_004.text: The ninth tread had a different problem. Its date mark matched the ledger, but the outer edge lifted under Ma's controlled probe. The engineer was called before anybody walked farther. Lin held the barrier from the safe landing while another assistant redirected traffic. Nobody asked her to reinforce the board with qi. A temporary human brace would have hidden the defect and kept the stair in service on an unexplained load. She watched the waiting workers change routes and understood that a useful discovery could still make a morning worse.

mine_p02_stairs_005.speaker: narrator
mine_p02_stairs_005.text: Fan arrived carrying the fastening specification. He looked beneath the tread from the permitted service opening and found a split around the outer fixing. He closed the flight pending replacement. The alternative stair was sound but longer. A basket carrier asked whether the added walking time would be recognized in the shift record. Fan referred the question to the forewoman rather than promising wages he could not authorize. Lin entered the time of closure and the named alternative. Those facts would support the workers' later account.

mine_p02_stairs_006.speaker: narrator
mine_p02_stairs_006.text: A younger worker tried to duck beneath the barrier because his lunch bundle remained below. Ma stopped him before he reached the doubtful tread. He said a bundle weighed nothing compared with a person. The observation was true and irrelevant to the act he proposed. The service attendant could retrieve it from the other landing. Lin offered to carry a message to that attendant from the cleared route. Ma approved the small errand. The worker got his lunch without having to make his body's weight part of the argument.

mine_p02_stairs_007.speaker: narrator
mine_p02_stairs_007.text: By the time Lin returned, the carpenter had brought replacement timber. He refused the first piece because its knot lay too close to the fastening position. The rejected piece went back into ordinary stock for a suitable use; it did not become firewood by dramatic decree. The next piece fitted the specified span. Lin waited outside the barrier while the carpenter and Fan completed their checks. She could admire their work without taking a turn with a tool she had not been employed or trained to use.

mine_p02_stairs_008.speaker: narrator
mine_p02_stairs_008.text: The flight reopened late in the morning. Ma asked Lin to read the new mark and the closure entry together. This time she identified every digit correctly. The repaired tread could carry its rated ordinary load after the engineer's acceptance. That did not certify the whole mine, the older stair, or a future flood. Lin signed only the assistant's observation line. She returned the chalk pencil and received the posted fee from the authorized clerk. Both transactions were small enough to finish before noon.

mine_p02_stairs_009.speaker: narrator
mine_p02_stairs_009.text: At the wash basin, the basket carrier told Lin that the longer route had made his ankle ache. He did not blame the new tread. He wanted the forewoman to understand that a safe diversion still had a cost. Lin said she could confirm the closure time, not diagnose his ankle or price his pain. He asked her to write the time clearly. She did. The account would contain an actual extra walk rather than an invented injury, and the man could seek assessment on his own terms.

mine_p02_stairs_010.speaker: narrator
mine_p02_stairs_010.text: Ma joined them with her sleeves wet to the elbows. She said the flight's old squeak had warned her less reliably than people imagined. Sometimes sound changed because dampness swelled a board; sometimes a quiet board split. Lin thought of the ticking seam and looked toward the gallery. Ma followed her gaze, then asked whether she wanted the last heel of bread. They ate it outside the closed work lane. Lin's first mine observation concerned a replaceable tread and the people who had to walk farther while it was replaced.

mine_clearance_air.speaker: narrator
mine_clearance_air.text: Lin accepted the ventilation recording turn. Ou Sheng handed her a ruled sheet with spaces for time, indicator position, location and his own inspection mark. She was to read from the cleared side of each station and leave controls untouched. A narrow red cord separated the observers from the valve handles. Lin asked what counted as an unreadable indicator. Ou demonstrated with a scratched practice face. When the position could not be distinguished, she would write that condition and call him instead of choosing a convenient number.

mine_p02_air_002.speaker: narrator
mine_p02_air_002.text: The first indicator stood near the receiving gallery's drain. Its feather moved in a weak but steady draft. Ou checked it against the comparison station and entered his finding beside Lin's observation. He did not claim the feather measured every gas a mine could contain. Other instruments and ordinary inspections served different purposes. Lin had seen cultivators use one bright response as proof of an entire environment. The separate stations made that habit look less impressive. A reading answered the question its instrument had been prepared to ask.

mine_p02_air_003.speaker: narrator
mine_p02_air_003.text: At the next alcove, a worker had hung a wet coat on the red cord. The garment blocked Lin's view but had not touched a valve. Ou had it moved to the drying rack and checked the station again. The worker complained that the rack was farther from his tea. Lin understood the wish to keep possessions close and the way a harmless convenience could interfere with somebody else's task. She recorded the obstruction, its removal and the repeat reading. She did not turn the coat into evidence of sabotage.

mine_p02_air_004.speaker: narrator
mine_p02_air_004.text: The third feather fluttered against its stop and then rested. Lin waited through the agreed observation interval. Ou watched from beside her. He asked what she had seen before offering his own description, so she could not simply repeat his answer. She described the movement and the pause. He compared the paired station, found an inconsistency, and closed the adjacent access pending a separate inspection. The visitors behind them were moved back. Lin's written line did not diagnose the cause, but it had helped preserve the actual sequence.

mine_p02_air_005.speaker: narrator
mine_p02_air_005.text: A supplier's messenger wanted to cross the closed access with a small parcel. He said his delivery had already been delayed at the outer gate. Ou directed him to the receiving clerk, who could accept it from the surface route if its recipient agreed. No urgency changed the air reading. The messenger looked at Lin's cultivation badge as though it might provide a different answer. She told him she had neither authority over the closure nor a technique that could make unknown air safe to breathe.

mine_p02_air_006.speaker: narrator
mine_p02_air_006.text: The inspector arrived with instruments Lin had not been allowed to use. Ou described the discrepant observations without announcing a cause. The inspector examined the service duct from the cleared side and found a loose packing panel interfering with the intended flow. An ordinary maintenance crew would secure it with the section isolated. Lin remained outside the work lane. The repair did not need her reserve. It needed a panel, the right fastening, and people who knew how to reach it without defeating the isolation they depended on.

mine_p02_air_007.speaker: narrator
mine_p02_air_007.text: While they waited, Ou showed Lin the maintenance calendar. One panel check had been moved after a shipment failed to arrive. That did not prove the missed check caused today's fault. It did identify a changed condition worth examining. Lin copied the public reference and left the crew names and private shift notes closed. The inspector would decide which sources belonged in the technical account. Ou said the most difficult part of recording was often resisting a sentence which made separate facts fit too neatly.

mine_p02_air_008.speaker: narrator
mine_p02_air_008.text: The panel was secured before noon. The inspector repeated the permitted checks and reopened the adjacent access only after accepting the results. Lin entered the reopening time beneath the closure time. A worker asked if the earlier feather's pause had meant they were already poisoned. The inspector explained the limits of the indicator and directed health concerns to the clinician. Lin watched the worker listen. An honest boundary was less comforting than a dramatic assurance, but it left him with a usable next action.

mine_p02_air_009.speaker: narrator
mine_p02_air_009.text: Ou counted the sheet's entries with Lin and corrected one location label. She had named the alcove after the nearest lamp instead of its posted station number. The distinction mattered because a later reader might not find the same lamp in the same place. She rewrote the label while keeping the correction visible. The authorized clerk paid the assistant's fee. Lin returned the unused pencil. Her work had produced an observation record and a temporary access change, not possession of the station or a standing right to its readings.

mine_p02_air_010.speaker: narrator
mine_p02_air_010.text: At the surface, the air tasted of bread smoke and damp stone. Ou took an ordinary deep breath without calling it practice. He said people who spent their shifts below often noticed the day's weather first through what others brought on their coats. Lin thought about the wet garment on the cord. A miner carried rain underground as a personal inconvenience; the station read a local flow; neither told the entire story of the mountain. She bought a small bun and ate it slowly before the next appointment.

mine_clearance_records.speaker: narrator
mine_clearance_records.text: Lin accepted the ticket comparison turn. Ren Tao cleared one end of the desk and brought yesterday's public duty board, numbered task tickets and the permitted incident register. Private wage pages stayed in a locked drawer. The comparison concerned who had been assigned, which authorized task was completed, and where a ticket's number could be found. It did not authorize Lin to decide wages or read somebody's illness notes. She washed the red grit from her hands before touching the first sheet.

mine_p02_records_002.speaker: narrator
mine_p02_records_002.text: The early tickets matched readily. A timber delivery had reached its named receiver; an empty-cart turn ended at the surface yard; two lamp attendants had exchanged their posts under the recorded supervisor's approval. Ren asked Lin to read each task in full rather than matching only names. A person could hold several tickets during one day. Treating the name as the whole event would confuse completed work with another assignment which had not begun. Lin saw how an efficient shortcut could erase the very difference their comparison existed to preserve.

mine_p02_records_003.speaker: narrator
mine_p02_records_003.text: The first discrepancy concerned a worker called Su E. Her morning ticket had been entered beneath the afternoon column because the ink on its time mark had run. The task itself was complete and the receiver's mark was legible. Ren did not shift it quietly. He asked the receiver to confirm the time against the delivery register and left a correction line for both sources. Lin held the place with a clean strip of paper while they checked. Su's work needed an accurate record, not another opportunity to prove that she had done it.

mine_p02_records_004.speaker: narrator
mine_p02_records_004.text: Su arrived while the comparison was still open. She looked at Lin, then at the locked drawer, and asked which part of her pay a visitor had been reading. Ren showed the permitted pages and explained the limited task. Su read them herself before agreeing that Lin could record the corrected public reference. Lin disliked being suspected and recognized that her discomfort did not create Su's consent. She thanked the worker for checking. The room settled after the question had been answered, rather than after somebody demanded trust.

mine_p02_records_005.speaker: narrator
mine_p02_records_005.text: A second ticket bore yesterday's date but described a valve inspection scheduled for today. Its holder had copied the wrong line from his task board. The inspector had not signed it, and the duty board still showed the work pending. Lin first thought the discrepancy meant a missed inspection. Ren asked her to retain the difference between an inaccurate issued ticket and a falsely recorded completion. They contacted the issuer, cancelled the mistaken sheet visibly, and produced the correctly dated ticket without awarding work which had not happened.

mine_p02_records_006.speaker: narrator
mine_p02_records_006.text: The issuer blamed poor light in the ticket room. Ren examined the lamp placement instead of accepting or dismissing the explanation at once. A shelf cast a shadow over the date column. Moving the shelf required the room custodian's approval because another worker used its space. Lin waited while that worker finished counting nails. The shelf moved afterward, the lamp stayed within its safe clearance, and the date column became easier to read. A small environmental repair could support responsibility without making the earlier error vanish.

mine_p02_records_007.speaker: narrator
mine_p02_records_007.text: The final unmatched number belonged to a stair closure recorded after the morning board had been copied. Ren found the engineer's signed instruction in the incident register. The workers diverted to another route had not abandoned their duties. Lin wrote the instruction's reference beside the unmatched number. She could not decide whether additional walking merited a separate payment. The wage reviewer would receive the actual closure interval and worker submissions. Su said that was better than being described as late when the short stair had been barred.

mine_p02_records_008.speaker: narrator
mine_p02_records_008.text: Before closing the comparison, Ren read the disputed entries aloud to the people whose public task records were affected. One man corrected the spelling of his receiver's name. Another asked to submit a written account later, after his shift. Neither response was treated as hostility. Lin watched the clerk preserve space for the later account without delaying the ordinary release of already confirmed work. A record could remain incomplete in one particular respect while still becoming useful in the parts which had been checked.

mine_p02_records_009.speaker: narrator
mine_p02_records_009.text: Lin signed the assistant's comparison line and returned the clean place strip to its tray. The authorized clerk paid the posted fee. Ren made clear that the payment bought today's bounded turn, not future access to the locked wage drawer. She had learned where the public task references lived and how corrections were entered. That knowledge would help her ask a better question later. It would not let her answer private questions on behalf of people who had only consented to a morning comparison.

mine_p02_records_010.speaker: narrator
mine_p02_records_010.text: Outside the ticket room, Su was trying to mend a split basket rim with ordinary cord. Lin asked whether she wanted help holding it. Su agreed. For several minutes neither spoke about the register. The cord made a rough but serviceable join for the basket's light load. Su thanked Lin and said she had worried about her task mark because a landlord never accepted a promise that paperwork would eventually catch up. Lin knew that kind of deadline. The corrected number would reach the wage reviewer before the next scheduled account.

mine_p02_shared_001.speaker: narrator
mine_p02_shared_001.text: At noon the three assistant turns ended. Lin returned to the receiving alcove with her own completed record, while the other leads kept their separate work. The common clearance did not expand to include everything she had heard about during the morning. Fan checked her visitor card, its escort condition, and the next appointment. The card gave access to the cleared gallery on the stated visits. Closed headings, machine controls and privately held papers remained outside it. She folded it beside her ordinary travel notes rather than wearing it like a rank.

mine_p02_shared_002.speaker: narrator
mine_p02_shared_002.text: Qiao had slept for part of the morning and returned looking less brittle. She asked Lin what had changed during the turn. Lin named the actual observation and the relevant authority. The forewoman listened before looking at the completed sheet. When Lin finished, Qiao asked what she had not been qualified to decide. That answer took longer. The exercise was not a trap. Qiao wanted to know whether a new assistant understood why a useful observation could leave another person's judgment necessary.

mine_p02_shared_003.speaker: narrator
mine_p02_shared_003.text: The receiving gallery had been built around an older natural opening. At one end, the wall kept a rounded shape which no mason had cut. Water shone there in a narrow black line. Lin had imagined the name Vermilion Hollows meant a vast red cavern. From the cleared path she saw pale stone, old repairs and the occasional rusty stain. A place could carry a dramatic name while its daily work consisted of keeping rain outside a cupboard and stopping wheels from entering the wrong lane.

mine_p02_shared_004.speaker: narrator
mine_p02_shared_004.text: Ma brought the visitor helmets to the storage rack. One had a torn inner strap. Qiao set it aside for replacement rather than offering it to the smallest visitor. Lin tried her own strap with ordinary fingers. It held the helmet steady without hurting her jaw. Fan said the fitting was part of clearance, not a test of endurance. If a strap caused pain, the wearer should ask for another fit. Lin remembered how often she had treated discomfort as a private problem which work expected her to solve silently.

mine_p02_shared_005.speaker: narrator
mine_p02_shared_005.text: A lunch cart arrived with soup, barley cakes and a covered pot of pickled greens. Its owner counted the ordered bowls against the receiving sheet. Visitors bought their own meals unless a particular accepted work agreement included one. Lin paid for a bowl from her purse. She did not assume the morning's assistant fee entitled her to the mine's food. Qiao took her meal in a patched bowl which she had left at the kitchen. The cook recognized it without asking which realm its owner had reached.

mine_p02_shared_006.speaker: narrator
mine_p02_shared_006.text: The soup contained turnip and a little dried mushroom. Lin ate at a surface bench beside a lamp attendant whose hands were stained with soot. He asked whether she could maintain six lights at once because she had six paired routes. She explained that the route count did not give each hand a separate mind or make ordinary lamps her proper task. A prepared small talisman might receive a permitted input within tested limits. Today's mine lights were maintained by people, oil and schedules. The attendant seemed relieved to keep his profession.

mine_p02_shared_007.speaker: narrator
mine_p02_shared_007.text: He told her that a visitor last year had offered to brighten the whole gallery for a demonstration. The offer had ended when the visitor asked who would supply fuel and replace a damaged lamp. Lin asked whether anyone had been hurt. He said the demonstration never proceeded. She did not turn that refusal into a tale of cowardice. It had prevented an unbudgeted experiment from entering a workplace. The attendant finished his cake and left at the time recorded for his return.

mine_p02_shared_008.speaker: narrator
mine_p02_shared_008.text: After lunch Fan led the visitors to the gallery's permitted viewing end. The boundary was a substantial rail with a latched service opening. Lin could see the beginning of a lower haul route, then darkness beyond a turn. She could not see the seam whose sounds had reached the entrance. A boy visiting his mother asked whether the mine went all the way through the mountain. Fan said it did not. The boy looked disappointed until his mother pointed out that going home required much less distance.

mine_p02_shared_009.speaker: narrator
mine_p02_shared_009.text: The engineer described the ordinary evacuation route before discussing any ore. Its destination was the surface assembly yard. If the primary path closed, the attendant would direct people to the inspected alternative. Nobody should follow a noise into an unknown opening or leave the escort to retrieve a possession. Lin repeated the instruction with the other visitors. The boy repeated it too quickly, making his mother laugh. Fan had him name the actual assembly gate, and his answer became slower and correct.

mine_p02_shared_010.speaker: narrator
mine_p02_shared_010.text: A visitor asked if a cultivator could hold the roof while others escaped. Fan said no visitor was assigned that role. Mine supports had known ordinary ratings and inspection requirements. An improvised qi brace could fail when its operator's route failed, conceal a dangerous load, or obstruct the crew's planned work. Lin felt the question land near her. She had once liked being imagined as an answer. Here the safer answer left her walking with everyone else, knowing which gate to use.

mine_p02_shared_011.speaker: narrator
mine_p02_shared_011.text: From the viewing end, a small grey moth crossed the lamp's light and settled on the rail. Its wings looked dusted with metal. Fan asked the visitors to leave it alone. The wildlife observer had requested notes about sightings near the cleared gallery, and nobody had authorized collecting specimens today. The moth neither spoke nor pointed toward treasure. It moved once when the boy shifted his boot. Lin could be curious without making the creature's presence into an instruction addressed especially to her.

mine_p02_shared_012.speaker: narrator
mine_p02_shared_012.text: Qiao returned with the week's open assistant positions. She placed the list on a public table where workers could read it before visitors. Lin was not being recruited into underground extraction. Available duties included surface copying, receiving checks and light preparation under named leads. Pay, hours and any included meals were written beside each. A role could be declined. The list did not contain a practice allowance or a promise that cultivation would become part of every task. Lin decided to read it at the next appointment rather than answer while still wearing the helmet.

mine_p02_shared_013.speaker: narrator
mine_p02_shared_013.text: One worker asked why visitors were being offered any paid turns while local people wanted more hours. Qiao showed the waiting list and the order of offers. The bounded morning turn had gone to Lin after the listed local applicants had selected other available duties or declined that particular interval. The worker checked the names without reading private wage pages. He still disliked the arrangement. Qiao noted his objection for the scheduled staffing discussion. An explanation of the process did not require him to approve its outcome.

mine_p02_shared_014.speaker: narrator
mine_p02_shared_014.text: Lin felt the familiar urge to surrender her fee to prove she had not taken anything from anybody. She stopped before offering. The payment had covered work she actually completed under the posted terms. Giving it away would not resolve the staffing dispute, and a grand gesture might make the worker responsible for reassuring her. She kept the coins and listened to his concern. Later she could decide what work to accept with the waiting list in view. Today's payment did not need a public performance.

mine_p02_shared_015.speaker: narrator
mine_p02_shared_015.text: The worker's name was Deng Huan. He had spent the winter on timber carrying and wanted a lighter turn while his shoulder recovered. The mine had offered a clinician appointment and temporary duties, but he doubted they would last. Lin asked whether he wanted his concern recorded beside the staffing objection. He said yes to that sentence and no to details of his shoulder. She wrote exactly the allowed concern. Qiao read it back. Deng took a copy with the public meeting date.

mine_p02_shared_016.speaker: narrator
mine_p02_shared_016.text: Near the outer gate, Fan showed Lin where the mine's ordinary instruments were issued. Each item had a responsible holder and a return line. Their ratings differed. A lamp used to illuminate a walk did not certify air; a sounding tool used on exposed timber did not diagnose rock behind a wall. Lin recognized the pattern from other workplaces and still found herself wanting a single instrument which would settle all questions. Fan said such an instrument would make its owner's mistake enormous.

mine_p02_shared_017.speaker: narrator
mine_p02_shared_017.text: He let her handle an unissued practice marker at the surface bench. Its ordinary pointer moved when the bench tilted. There was no qi input. She saw how an apparently clear change could come from placement rather than the condition someone intended to measure. Fan then levelled the bench and had her repeat the comparison. The pointer steadied. Lin asked whether the mine kept both readings. He said training notes should preserve the mistaken setup when it explained a correction. A clean page was not always the clearest account.

mine_p02_shared_018.speaker: narrator
mine_p02_shared_018.text: A bell sounded from the yard. It announced the scheduled change of lamp attendants, not an emergency. The visitors looked toward one another before their escort explained it. Fan reviewed the actual emergency signal and had the attendant demonstrate its distinct pattern under the announced test condition. Lin heard the difference in that place. She did not assume she would recognize it through every wall. The escort would guide visitors, and the crew's practised response did not depend on a stranger interpreting an unfamiliar echo perfectly.

mine_p02_shared_019.speaker: narrator
mine_p02_shared_019.text: The boy asked whether the bell wire could break. Fan said it could, and showed the alternate reporting arrangement and the checks which kept that risk visible. The answer made the boy quiet. His mother took his hand. Lin watched a child encounter a machine's limit without being told that adults had eliminated every danger. The engineer did not linger over fear. He led them back by the inspected route while the yard attendant marked the signal test complete.

mine_p02_shared_020.speaker: narrator
mine_p02_shared_020.text: At the gate, every visitor returned the helmet issued to them. The attendant counted them, set the damaged spare aside, and closed the visitor sheet. Lin kept her own card. Qiao asked her to bring it to the next receiving appointment and to seek a fresh instruction if the route board had changed. A clearance existed in a particular workplace at a particular time. It was not a memory she could spend indefinitely. Lin liked having the card and knew she would have to resist treating its survival in her pack as proof of continuing permission.

mine_p02_shared_021.speaker: narrator
mine_p02_shared_021.text: The afternoon rain began while she walked toward the lodging lane. Water struck the gallery roof behind her with a different rhythm from the ticking she had heard inside. Lin waited beneath a shop awning without calling either sound a message. The shopkeeper moved a basin to catch a leak and asked her to stand farther from the flour sacks. She did. A mountain full of rare ore had not stopped a roof from needing an ordinary basin in the right place.

mine_p02_shared_022.speaker: narrator
mine_p02_shared_022.text: A tailor sat inside the shop repairing a miner's sleeve. The cloth had worn through where it rubbed against a basket strap. Lin asked what the repair would cost before touching the garment. The tailor said it belonged to the miner and the price had already been agreed. Conversation did not give Lin a role in that agreement. She bought a short length of thread for her own cuff instead. The rain kept both women near the door long enough to discuss the quality of needles.

mine_p02_shared_023.speaker: narrator
mine_p02_shared_023.text: The tailor, Hu Sa, had a brother working the lower haul route. She disliked the mine and relied on its wages. Lin asked whether those feelings made repairs harder to price. Hu said the cloth had the same hole either way. She could mend it well and still wish her brother had another trade. The answer stayed with Lin because it did not offer a neat choice between affection and criticism. A person might need the workplace whose failures she knew most clearly.

mine_p02_shared_024.speaker: narrator
mine_p02_shared_024.text: When the rain eased, Lin stopped at the public notice shelter. The next staffing discussion, supplier receiving interval and clinic appointments appeared on separate sheets. She copied only the dates relevant to her own possible work. On the clinic sheet, Chen Ai's name was followed by qualifications and a note about urgent assessment. There was no offer of spiritual healing. Lin had no new injury to present that day. She wanted to know where ordinary care was available before an emergency made the question harder to ask.

mine_p02_shared_025.speaker: narrator
mine_p02_shared_025.text: The lodging keeper gave her a dry cloth for the mud near the entrance and asked whether she had decided on a longer stay. Lin said she had only the next appointments. The keeper showed rates for a bed, meals and a weekly arrangement, each with its own end condition. Nothing had been reserved by virtue of a cultivation title. Lin paid for the already agreed night and deferred the longer commitment until she could compare it with actual work. The keeper accepted that answer without treating uncertainty as dishonesty.

mine_p02_shared_026.speaker: narrator
mine_p02_shared_026.text: In the room, she mended her cuff while the afternoon light faded. The thread was slightly darker than the old seam. She could have waited to find a closer match, but the tear would spread during ordinary use. Lin made a repair whose difference remained visible. It had no relation to the unopened governing and conception bridges she had been thinking about for months. She was glad to have one small task she could finish without an examiner, a mineral sample or a future promise.

mine_p02_shared_027.speaker: narrator
mine_p02_shared_027.text: Her cultivation notes stayed closed until she had eaten. Then she wrote today's ordinary work beside her existing practice record, keeping the columns separate. A valid mine observation did not add usable reserve. Her maintained sixth stage did not authorize the engineer's work. She noted the need for sleep before any measured practice and left tomorrow's figures blank. The page was less satisfying without a new number, but it preserved the distinction between a day lived and a capacity demonstrated.

mine_p02_shared_028.speaker: narrator
mine_p02_shared_028.text: She heard a cart pass below the window and imagined the basket carrier's longer walk, the delayed parcel, the worker whose ticket date had run. Only one assistant turn had been hers; the other work continued through its own people. Lin did not write every event as her accomplishment. She could learn from an account without occupying it. That thought made her notes shorter and her understanding of the mine less tidy. A workplace was not waiting for a visitor to become its only meaningful witness.

mine_p02_shared_029.speaker: narrator
mine_p02_shared_029.text: Her room account marked the end of the arrival arrangement. Tonight's bed was hers to pay for. Lin counted the separate coins before closing her purse, preserving the completed receiving wage instead of spending it twice.

mine_p02_shared_030.speaker: narrator
mine_p02_shared_030.text: Before sleeping, Lin placed the clearance card beside the room key. Both could be lost. Both opened limited things. Neither belonged on a cultivation chart. The room smelled faintly of damp wool despite the dry bedding. Somewhere down the lane a child was rehearsing the mine bell pattern with a spoon and cup. His mother corrected him once and then asked him to eat. Lin smiled, turned down her ordinary lamp, and left the next appointment to a body which had actually rested.
